channel.title: Web3 Hub
channel.description: Web3 Hub reports crypto news: Bitcoin and Ethereum, exchanges, DeFi protocols, stablecoins, regulation, security incidents and network upgrades.

item.title: How to Budget Monero Fees for an XMR Bridge
item.description: Budget an XMR bridge by separating the source-chain fee, swap spread, service charge and Monero withdrawal; compare the final receive quote before sending.

item.title: Compare Cross-Chain Swaps by the Amount You Receive
item.description: Compare routes by the amount expected to arrive after swap fees, bridge costs and slippage; quotes can change before execution, so check destination details too.

item.title: V2 vs V3 pools: how to choose between them
item.description: V2 spreads liquidity across all prices; V3 concentrates it in a chosen range. The right pool depends on how much monitoring and price risk you can manage.

item.title: How to Receive XMR in Your Wallet After a Swap
item.description: To receive XMR after a swap, copy a fresh Monero subaddress, check the destination network and amount, then track the payout until your wallet syncs.

item.title: Crypto hacks hit $772M in September, CertiK dashboard shows
item.description: CertiK’s updated dashboard puts September’s crypto security losses at $772.4 million, led by Bitget and Liquid, after more than $270 million was returned.

item.title: SEC proposes crypto custody rules for advisers and funds
item.description: The SEC proposed rules letting advisers and funds use state trust companies or self-custody for some crypto assets, with safeguards under federal securities laws.

item.title: XMR bridge: how to move Monero between networks
item.description: An XMR bridge swaps Monero for an asset on another blockchain; learn how wallet-based routes work, what changes hands and which checks matter before sending.

item.title: How to Estimate Energy for Arithmetic-Heavy TVM Calls
item.description: Estimate TRON Energy by counting executed TVM opcodes, modeling loop and input effects, then checking the result against a current node simulation.

item.title: How to Estimate the Cost of a TRON USDT Payout
item.description: Estimate a TRON USDT payout by simulating the exact transfer, pricing its Energy shortfall at the current chain rate and adding any Bandwidth burn.

item.title: Read OTC Liquidity on an XMR Bridge Before You Swap
item.description: OTC liquidity on an XMR bridge is dealer inventory behind a quote; compare executable size, net rate, fees and settlement conditions before sending funds.

item.title: XMR swaps need separate memo support for exchange payouts
item.description: An XMR swap can reach memo-required exchange accounts only when its payout flow carries the destination memo; the Monero deposit and recipient tag serve different networks.

item.title: How to Fix a Crypto Wallet Showing the Wrong Network
item.description: A wallet’s network label can differ from the app’s connection or token display; check the chain, app permissions and verified network details before retrying.

item.title: Blackhole swap routes: when lower fees lose to shallow pools
item.description: A Blackhole swap route is only cheaper when fee savings outweigh price impact; compare quoted output, usable pool depth and every hop before signing.

item.title: Low Swap Quote? Check Price Impact Before You Trade
item.description: A low swap quote can signal that your trade will move a pool’s price; compare price impact, fees, route depth and slippage before approving the transaction.

item.title: Avalanche swaps: set slippage against the minimum output
item.description: Avalanche swap slippage tolerance sets the minimum output a trade can deliver; compare it with liquidity, price impact and token volatility before signing.

item.title: AMM Pool Creation: Why a Duplicate Pair Can Fail
item.description: An AMM can reject a duplicate pair because factories key pools by token addresses and configuration; check the factory, chain and fee tier before creating one.

item.title: Base swap slippage: set the limit to fit the trade
item.description: Set slippage to the smallest tolerance that lets a Base swap execute: it caps how far output may fall, while liquidity and price movement determine the quote.

item.title: What a Wrapped Token Represents After a Cross-Chain Transfer
item.description: Wrapped tokens represent assets moved between chains through lock-and-mint or burn-and-release systems; backing and redemption determine what holders can recover.

item.title: Bridge routes trade speed for settlement certainty
item.description: Bridge routes can deliver tokens sooner through liquidity providers, while canonical exits follow the source chain’s settlement rules and may take longer.

item.title: Four decisions shape live oracle slippage protection
item.description: A live oracle guard needs a trusted reference, a freshness limit, a price band and a failure rule; each choice trades execution access against loss control.
